kevin (customer): hey team — after we migrated clients to the new SDK, our tool calls started failing in prod. getting: "ToolResponse schema mismatch: missing 'result' field" and some enum errors. using OpenAI-style tool calling. anyone seen this?

kevin (customer): repro snippet: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-redwood","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Find the price of widget x"}],"tool_call":{"name":"web_search","args":"{"q":"widget x price"}"}}'```

sujay (support): thanks @kevin — can you confirm which SDK version you upgraded from and whether you used openai-compatible request shape before? :eyes:

kevin (customer): we were on our fork of openai-js v4.1.1. we switched to redwood/sdk-js v1.2.0 but kept the same request shape in the backend. previously we sent the payload exactly as in the curl above (name: web_search, args as string).

sujay (support): quick summary of what I'm seeing in our logs when I replayed a similar request: ``ERROR tool_call validation: expected top-level tool_call.name to match registered tool enum ['search','calculator'], got 'web_search' ; expected tool_call.arguments to be an object but got a string; downstream plugin adapter attempted json-parse and failed -> rejected``

sujay (support): root causes likely 2 things: 1) enum/name mismatch — openai-client used a tool called "web_search" but your model/tool registry in Redwood expects canonical names (eg "search"). 2) argument shape — Redwood currently requires arguments to be a JSON object (not a JSON-string). Some OpenAI-style clients send stringified args.

kevin (customer): so is this a config mismatch on our end or a breaking change in the SDK? we have hundreds of requests per minute — prod impact.

sujay (support): short: both. SDK and model reg changes mean the request that used to be tolerated now fails stricter validation. we can do immediate mitigations: a) server-side compat parsing for stringified args + alias mapping for common tool name variants (e.g., web_search -> search) b) docs + SDK patch to normalize shapes. i'll escalate to eng for a hotfix shim.

sujay (support): repro steps i used (safe replay): 1) curl payload with tool_call.name=web_search and tool_call.args as string 2) saw validation error 3) replay with tool_call.name=search and tool_call.arguments as object -> success.

maria (eng): pinged — thanks for the clear repro @sujay. quick notes from runtime side: we intentionally tightened tool_call schema to avoid ambiguity in routing and to keep tool adapters pure typed objects. That said, compatibility shim is reasonable for short-term.

maria (eng): proposed fix items: 1) add tolerant parser at the API edge that will: - accept tool_call.arguments as string and attempt JSON.parse (safe) - accept alias tool names from a configurable map (web_search -> search, search_engine -> search) 2) add a non-default compatibility flag in tenant settings so we don't alter behavior for tenants who rely on strict typing 3) add regression tests and note the security parsing boundary (only JSON.parse, no eval)

maria (eng): quick ETA: can do a staged patch today for the parser + alias map in the edge validator (low risk) and a more formal SDK change tomorrow to normalize outgoing payloads. will open a PR and attach logs.

kevin (customer): that sounds great. can you apply the tenant-level compat flag for our org? id is org_45321. need minimal downtime.

sujay (support): can do — i'll request the compat flag toggle after eng approves the edge patch. in meantime, workaround for your team: change tool_call.name to the canonical tool name (search) and send arguments as a JSON object (not string). example payload: ```{"tool_call":{"name":"search","arguments":{"q":"widget x price"}}}```

kevin (customer): copying that to our deploy queue now. thanks. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy request #D-9987 created for org_45321 compat-change. ETA 10m.

maria (eng): started a minimal compat-shim branch: will post PR link in ~20m. note: we'll only auto-parse string args when Content-Type is application/json and length < 64kb to avoid accidental huge-parsing CPU spikes.

sujay (support): flagged this as P1 — customer-facing error, high traffic. added to incidents channel and notified oncall.

kevin (customer): confirmed workaround deployed on our side. initial traffic looks green. will update if we see anything else. thanks all. :bow:
